---
id: 'auth-third-party-scalekit'
title: 'Scalekit'
subtitle: 'Use Scalekit with your Supabase project'
---

Scalekit authenticates your users and issues an access token. Supabase uses that token to authorize requests to your project. You can use Scalekit alongside Supabase Auth, or on its own.

## Getting started

1. In the Scalekit Dashboard, under **Developers**, open **Settings**, then **API Credentials**. Copy **Environment URL**. When **API Credentials** is its own item, open it under **Developers**.
2. In the Supabase Dashboard, add that URL as a **Custom OIDC** integration. See [Add the integration](#add-the-integration).
3. On the Scalekit access token, add a `role` claim set to `authenticated`. See [Add the role claim](#add-the-role-claim).
4. On your server, return that access token from the Supabase client library. See [Set up the Supabase client library](#set-up-the-supabase-client-library).

## Add the integration

In the Supabase Dashboard, go to **Authentication** > **Sign In / Providers** > [**Third-Party Auth**](/dashboard/project/_/auth/third-party).

1. Click **Add provider** and select **Custom OIDC**.
2. In **Issuer URL**, enter the Scalekit **Environment URL**.
3. Click **Add provider**.

The integration appears in the Third-Party Auth list with that issuer URL. To remove the integration, delete it from that list.

Scalekit signs access tokens with RS256 and includes a `kid` header. Supabase loads the signing keys from `<Environment URL>/.well-known/openid-configuration`. **Issuer URL** is the Environment URL.

To add the same issuer from a terminal, create a [personal access token](/docs/guides/platform/personal-access-tokens). Call the [create third-party auth integration](/docs/reference/api/v1-create-project-tpa-integration) endpoint. Set `oidc_issuer_url` to the Environment URL.

## Add the role claim

Supabase reads the `role` claim on each JWT. It uses that value as the Postgres role for the Data API, Storage, and Realtime. For a signed-in user, set `role` to `authenticated`. A request with no `role` claim runs as `anon`.

A Scalekit access token includes `roles` as a list. Supabase uses the string claim `role` as the Postgres role. Add `role` in Token Claims.

In the Scalekit Dashboard, go to **Configure** > **Authentication** > **Token Claims**.

1. Click **Add custom claim**.
2. In **Claim key**, enter `role`.
3. In **Expression**, enter `authenticated`.
4. Click **Add**.

Enter `authenticated` as the whole expression. Keep the existing `roles` claim.

## Set up the Supabase client library

Install `@scalekit-sdk/node` on your server. After the user signs in, exchange the authorization code in your server callback and store the `accessToken` string. The package sends your client secret, so run it on the server.

```typescript
import { Scalekit } from '@scalekit-sdk/node'

const scalekit = new Scalekit(
  '<SCALEKIT_ENVIRONMENT_URL>',
  '<SCALEKIT_CLIENT_ID>',
  '<SCALEKIT_CLIENT_SECRET>'
)

const { accessToken } = await scalekit.authenticateWithCode(code, redirectUri)
```

`code` is the value Scalekit sends to your redirect URI. Save `accessToken` in your server session.

Pass that stored string from the Supabase client library. Return `null` when no user is signed in.

```typescript
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'

const supabase = createClient(
  'https://<supabase-project>.supabase.co',
  'SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY',
  {
    accessToken: async () => {
      return storedAccessToken
    },
  }
)
```

`storedAccessToken` is the string you saved. `getSession()` and `currentUser()` return claims and expiry. Return the saved string here.

## Identify the user in Row Level Security

The `sub` claim identifies the user. `auth.uid()` casts `sub` to `uuid`, so it fails when `sub` is not a UUID. Read the claim directly instead.

Run the following SQL using the [SQL Editor](/dashboard/project/_/sql) in the Supabase Dashboard or with `psql` over a direct connection. To connect with `psql`, see [Direct connection](/docs/guides/database/connecting-to-postgres#direct-connection).

```sql
create policy "Users can read their own rows"
  on table_name
  for select
  to authenticated
  using (user_id = (select auth.jwt()->>'sub'));
```

Use a `text` column for `user_id`.

When the project trusts more than one issuer, also restrict policies by `iss`. See [Restrict access by issuer](/docs/guides/auth/third-party/custom-oidc#restrict-access-by-issuer).
